# Access Control Policy

## 1. Purpose

This Access Control Policy establishes the requirements and procedures for managing access to information systems and data within **Simtenant Alpha Aerospace LLC (synthetic)** in accordance with NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 (Family 3.1) and CMMC L2 requirements.

## 2. Scope

This policy applies to all information systems, applications, and data repositories that process, store, or transmit Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) within the single_enclave boundary operated by Simtenant Alpha Aerospace LLC (synthetic).


**Estimated in-scope users:** 85
**Estimated in-scope endpoints:** 85

## 3. Roles and Responsibilities

| Role | Name | Responsibility |
|------|------|----------------|
| Information System Security Officer | Fixture Person One, ISSO, person.one@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Enforce access control policies and monitor compliance |
| System Owner | Fixture Person Two, System Owner, person.two@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Authorize access to systems and approve access requests |
| IT Director / CTO | Fixture Person Four, IT Director, person.four@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Maintain technical access control mechanisms |
| Compliance Officer | Fixture Person Three, Compliance Officer, person.three@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Audit access control effectiveness |

## 4. Policy Statements

### 4.1 Account Management (3.1.1, 3.1.2)

Simtenant Alpha Aerospace LLC (synthetic) shall limit information system access to authorized users, processes acting on behalf of authorized users, and devices.

- Access shall be granted based on the principle of least privilege
- All accounts shall be reviewed on a **Quarterly** basis
- Account lockout shall be enforced after **3** failed login attempts
- Accounts shall be locked for **15** minutes after lockout threshold is reached
- Primary identity management is performed through **entra_native** on the **gcc_high** tenant (simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us)

### 4.2 Access Enforcement (3.1.3, 3.1.4)

Access to CUI shall be controlled through:
- Role-based access control (RBAC)
- Conditional access policies following the **CA-{Number}-{Purpose}** naming convention
- Multi-factor authentication for all users accessing CUI

### 4.3 Separation of Duties (3.1.4)

Simtenant Alpha Aerospace LLC (synthetic) shall enforce separation of duties through:
- Distinct administrative and user accounts
- Privileged Identity Management (PIM) — **currently enabled**
- Segregated roles for security administration, system administration, and audit functions

### 4.4 Least Privilege (3.1.5, 3.1.6)

- Users shall be authorized only the minimum access necessary for their job functions
- Privileged accounts shall be limited to designated administrators
- CUI access shall require explicit authorization from the System Owner

### 4.5 Unsuccessful Logon Attempts (3.1.8)

The system shall limit unsuccessful logon attempts to **3** consecutive attempts within a 15-minute window. After exceeding the threshold, the account shall be locked for **15** minutes.

### 4.6 Session Management (3.1.10, 3.1.11)

- Session timeout shall be enforced after **15** minutes of inactivity
- Sessions shall be terminated upon user logoff
- Session locks shall require re-authentication

### 4.7 Remote Access (3.1.12, 3.1.13, 3.1.14)

- All remote access to CUI systems shall be monitored and controlled
- Remote access sessions shall use encrypted connections (TLS 1.2+)
- BYOD posture: **not_allowed**
- Personal devices are prohibited from accessing CUI

### 4.8 Wireless Access (3.1.16, 3.1.17)

- Wireless access to CUI systems shall be authenticated and encrypted
- Wireless access points shall be monitored for unauthorized connections

### 4.9 Mobile Device Access (3.1.18, 3.1.19)

- Mobile devices accessing CUI shall be enrolled in mobile device management
- Device enrollment type: **azure_ad_join**
- CUI shall be encrypted at rest on all mobile devices

### 4.10 External System Connections (3.1.20, 3.1.21, 3.1.22)

- Connections to external systems shall be authorized by the System Owner
- Publicly accessible information systems shall not contain CUI
- Collaboration mode: **teams_first**

## 5. Enforcement

Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment and/or contract.

## 6. Review

This policy shall be reviewed every **12** months. Next scheduled review: **2027-02-01**.

---

**Effective Date:** 2026-02-01
**NIST SP 800-171 Controls:** 3.1.1–3.1.22

## 1. Purpose

This policy establishes the security awareness and training requirements for all personnel of **Simtenant Alpha Aerospace LLC (synthetic)** who access information systems processing, storing, or transmitting Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), in accordance with NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 (Family 3.2) and CMMC L2 requirements.

## 2. Scope

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party personnel with access to CUI systems within the single_enclave boundary, including the cloud_only deployment posture operating in the gcc_high cloud environment.

## 3. Roles and Responsibilities

| Role | Name | Responsibility |
|------|------|----------------|
| ISSO | Fixture Person One, ISSO, person.one@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Develop and maintain training content |
| HR Representative | Fixture Person Five, HR Representative, person.five@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Track training completion and enforce compliance |
| System Owner | Fixture Person Two, System Owner, person.two@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Ensure role-based training for system users |
| Compliance Officer | Fixture Person Three, Compliance Officer, person.three@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Audit training program effectiveness |

## 4. Policy Statements

### 4.1 Security Awareness Training (3.2.1)

All personnel shall receive security awareness training:
- Upon initial hire or role assignment
- On an **annual** recurring basis
- When significant changes occur to information systems or policy

Training shall cover at minimum:
- CUI identification and handling procedures
- Phishing and social engineering awareness
- Password management and authentication requirements
- Incident reporting procedures
- Acceptable use of information systems
- Physical security responsibilities

#### Required DoD Course Catalog

The following courses are required for all CUI-access personnel. Courses are self-paced, free of charge, and delivered through government training portals.

| Course | Provider | Frequency | Audience | URL |
|--------|----------|-----------|----------|-----|
| DoD Cyber Awareness Challenge | DoD | Annual | All CUI-access personnel | https://cs.signal.army.mil |
| DoD Mandatory CUI Training | CDSE | Initial + Biennial | All CUI-access personnel | https://www.cdse.edu/Training/eLearning/ |
| CDSE Insider Threat Awareness (INT101.16) | CDSE | Annual | All CUI-access personnel | https://www.cdse.edu/Training/eLearning/ |

### 4.2 Role-Based Security Training (3.2.2)

Personnel with significant security responsibilities shall receive specialized training appropriate to their assigned roles:
- System administrators — secure configuration, patch management, log review
- Security personnel — incident response, vulnerability management, audit review
- Managers — risk management, policy enforcement, access authorization
- Developers — secure coding practices, SAST/DAST tools

#### Administrator-Track Course Requirements

System administrators shall complete the following additional courses annually, or an equivalent from CISA:

| Course | Provider | Frequency | Audience | URL |
|--------|----------|-----------|----------|-----|
| CDSE Cybersecurity Fundamentals | CDSE | Annual | System administrators | https://www.cdse.edu/Training/eLearning/ |

### 4.3 Insider Threat Awareness (3.2.3)

All personnel shall receive training on recognizing and reporting insider threats, including:
- Indicators of potential insider threat behavior
- Reporting mechanisms and points of contact
- Protection of whistleblowers and reporters

All personnel shall be trained on indicators of insider threat as defined in the CDSE INT101.16 curriculum. Training shall emphasize recognition of behavioral and technical indicators and the obligation to report.

Suspected insider threat indicators shall be reported to Fixture Person Six, IR Lead, person.six@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us within 24 hours of observation.

## 5. Training Records

All training completion records shall be maintained for **6** years per 6 years per 32 CFR 170.16 and made available for assessment purposes.

Training certificates shall be downloaded as PDF and stored in the individual's personnel record. Certificate retention follows the same retention period.

## 5A. Training Frequency and Anchor

Training cycles are anchored to the DoD fiscal year beginning October 1. Annual courses must be completed within each fiscal year cycle. Biennial courses must be completed within each two-year cycle from the date of initial completion.

> Course URLs verified as of 2026. Verify current availability at each training cycle.

## 6. Enforcement

Personnel who fail to complete required training within the specified timeframe shall have CUI system access disabled until training is completed and documented. Access suspension and restoration shall be documented in the Personnel card within the compliance tooling.

## 7. Review

This policy shall be reviewed every **12** months. Next scheduled review: **2027-02-01**.

# Audit and Accountability Policy

## 1. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements for audit logging, monitoring, and accountability within **Simtenant Alpha Aerospace LLC (synthetic)** in accordance with NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 (Family 3.3) and CMMC L2 requirements.

## 2. Scope

This policy applies to all information systems within the single_enclave boundary that process, store, or transmit CUI.

## 3. Roles and Responsibilities

| Role | Name | Responsibility |
|------|------|----------------|
| ISSO | Fixture Person One, ISSO, person.one@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Establish audit requirements and review audit logs |
| IT Director | Fixture Person Four, IT Director, person.four@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Implement and maintain audit infrastructure |
| System Owner | Fixture Person Two, System Owner, person.two@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Ensure systems generate required audit records |
| Compliance Officer | Fixture Person Three, Compliance Officer, person.three@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Verify audit compliance |

## 4. Policy Statements

### 4.1 Audit Event Creation (3.3.1)

The organization shall create and retain system audit logs sufficient to establish:
- What type of event occurred
- When the event occurred
- Where the event occurred
- Source of the event
- Outcome of the event
- Identity of individuals or subjects associated with the event

Auditable events include at minimum: login/logout, access to CUI, privilege changes, system configuration changes, account management actions, and failed access attempts.

### 4.2 Audit Correlation and Reporting (3.3.2)

Audit records from multiple sources shall be correlated to support investigation of security incidents.
- SIEM: Microsoft Sentinel workspace **simtenant-a-law-prod**
- Active data connectors: Azure Active Directory, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Microsoft Defender for Office 365, Microsoft Defender for Identity, Azure Activity, Windows Security Events

### 4.3 Audit Record Content (3.3.1, 3.3.2)

Audit records shall contain sufficient information to establish what occurred, when, where, the source, and the outcome.

### 4.4 Audit Storage and Retention (3.3.4)

- Audit logs shall be retained for a minimum of **365** days
- Audit storage capacity shall be managed to prevent storage exhaustion
- Alerts shall be generated when audit storage reaches 80% capacity

### 4.5 Audit Log Protection (3.3.3, 3.3.8)

- Audit logs shall be protected from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion
- Only designated security personnel shall have access to audit log management functions
- Audit log integrity shall be protected using tamper-evident mechanisms

### 4.6 Audit Review and Analysis (3.3.5)

- Audit logs shall be reviewed on a regular schedule (at minimum weekly)
- Automated alerting shall be configured for high-severity events
- Unusual or suspicious activity shall be investigated and documented

### 4.7 Audit Reduction and Report Generation (3.3.6)

The organization shall provide audit reduction and report generation capabilities to support after-the-fact investigations and on-demand compliance reporting.

### 4.8 Time Synchronization (3.3.7)

All systems shall synchronize clocks to a common authoritative time source to enable accurate audit record correlation.

### 4.9 Audit Process Protection (3.3.9)

Audit logging processes shall be protected from unauthorized shutdown or modification. System administrators shall not have the ability to disable auditing on CUI systems.

## 5. Enforcement

Disabling, circumventing, or tampering with audit controls is strictly prohibited and may result in disciplinary action.

## 6. Review

This policy shall be reviewed every **12** months. Next scheduled review: **2027-02-01**.

---

**Effective Date:** 2026-02-01
**NIST SP 800-171 Controls:** 3.3.1–3.3.9
**Policy Owner:** Fixture Person One, ISSO, person.one@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us

## 2. Scope

This policy applies to all information systems, software, and hardware within the single_enclave boundary, including cloud_only environments.

### 4.1 Baseline Configurations (3.4.1, 3.4.2)

- Baseline configurations shall be established, documented, and maintained for all information systems
- Configurations shall reflect the most restrictive mode consistent with operational requirements
- Baselines shall include operating system settings, application configurations, and network device configurations

### 4.2 Configuration Change Control (3.4.3, 3.4.4, 3.4.5)

- All changes to information systems shall be tracked, reviewed, and approved prior to implementation
- Security impact analyses shall be conducted for proposed changes
- Physical and logical access restrictions shall limit who can make changes to systems
- Changes to the CUI boundary or security configurations require documented approval from the System Owner

### 4.3 Least Functionality (3.4.6, 3.4.7, 3.4.8)

- Systems shall be configured to provide only essential capabilities
- Unnecessary functions, ports, protocols, and services shall be disabled
- Software installation shall be restricted to authorized personnel
- Application whitelisting or similar controls shall be implemented where feasible

### 4.4 Nonessential Programs (3.4.8)

Policies shall be defined for restricting the use of:
- Unauthorized software applications
- Non-essential system utilities
- Peer-to-peer applications
- Unauthorized browser extensions

### 4.5 User-Installed Software (3.4.9)

- Users shall not install software on organizational systems without prior authorization
- Software requests shall be submitted through the change management process
- An approved software list shall be maintained and reviewed periodically

# Identification and Authentication Policy

## 1. Purpose

This policy establishes identification and authentication requirements for **Simtenant Alpha Aerospace LLC (synthetic)** in accordance with NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 (Family 3.5) and CMMC L2 requirements.

## 2. Scope

This policy applies to all users, devices, and processes accessing information systems within the single_enclave boundary.

## 3. Roles and Responsibilities

| Role | Name | Responsibility |
|------|------|----------------|
| ISSO | Fixture Person One, ISSO, person.one@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Define authentication standards |
| IT Director | Fixture Person Four, IT Director, person.four@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Implement authentication mechanisms |
| System Owner | Fixture Person Two, System Owner, person.two@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Authorize user identities |

## 4. Policy Statements

### 4.1 User Identification (3.5.1, 3.5.2)

- Each user shall be assigned a unique identifier
- User identities shall be verified before granting system access
- Shared accounts are prohibited for CUI system access
- Identity provider: **entra_native** on gcc_high tenant (simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us)

### 4.2 Multi-Factor Authentication (3.5.3)

- Multi-factor authentication (MFA) shall be required for:
  - All access to CUI systems (local and remote)
  - All privileged account access
  - All remote access sessions
- MFA shall use at least two of: something you know, something you have, something you are

### 4.3 Replay-Resistant Authentication (3.5.4)

Authentication mechanisms shall employ replay-resistant techniques (e.g., time-based tokens, challenge-response, cryptographic authenticators).

### 4.4 Identifier Management (3.5.5, 3.5.6)

- User identifiers shall not be reused for a minimum of 2 years after account deletion
- Inactive accounts shall be disabled after 90 days of inactivity
- Temporary accounts shall have explicit expiration dates

### 4.5 Password Management (3.5.7, 3.5.8, 3.5.9, 3.5.10)

- Minimum password length: **14** characters
- Password complexity: combination of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters
- Password history: last **24** passwords shall not be reused
- Maximum password age: **60** days
- Passwords shall be stored using cryptographically secure hashing
- Default and vendor-supplied passwords shall be changed immediately upon installation

### 4.6 Authenticator Feedback (3.5.10)

Authentication feedback shall not reveal whether the identifier or the authenticator was incorrect (obscured error messages).

### 4.7 Cryptographic Authentication (3.5.11)

Cryptographic mechanisms shall be used to protect the confidentiality of authentication information during transmission.

## 5. Enforcement

Accounts that violate this policy (e.g., shared credentials, disabled MFA) shall be suspended pending investigation.

## 6. Review

This policy shall be reviewed every **12** months. Next scheduled review: **2027-02-01**.

---

**Effective Date:** 2026-02-01
**NIST SP 800-171 Controls:** 3.5.1–3.5.11

# Incident Response Policy

## 1. Purpose

This policy establishes the incident response requirements for **Simtenant Alpha Aerospace LLC (synthetic)** in accordance with NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 (Family 3.6) and CMMC L2 requirements.

## 4. Policy Statements

### 4.1 Incident Response Capability (3.6.1)

Simtenant Alpha Aerospace LLC (synthetic) shall maintain an operational incident response capability that includes:
- An incident response plan (see companion IRP document)
- Trained incident response personnel
- Regular testing of the incident response capability
- Defined roles and responsibilities for incident handling

### 4.2 Incident Tracking and Reporting (3.6.1, 3.6.2)

- All security incidents shall be tracked from detection through resolution
- Incidents involving CUI shall be reported to the ISSO within **72** hour(s) of discovery
- Incidents shall be reported to the DoD CUI Program and DIBCAC as required
- Incident reports shall include: description, timeline, systems affected, CUI impact, response actions, and lessons learned

### 4.3 Incident Response Testing (3.6.3)

- The incident response plan shall be tested at least annually
- Testing methods may include tabletop exercises, simulations, or full-scale exercises
- Test results shall be documented and used to improve the incident response plan

## 5. Incident Classification

| Severity | Description | Response Time |
|----------|-------------|---------------|
| Critical | Active CUI compromise or data exfiltration | Immediate |
| High | Potential CUI exposure or system compromise | Within 72 hour(s) |
| Medium | Policy violation or suspicious activity | Within 4 hours |
| Low | Minor security event, no CUI impact | Within 24 hours |

This policy shall be reviewed every **12** months. Next scheduled review: **2027-02-01**.

# Media Protection Policy

## 1. Purpose

This policy establishes requirements for protecting media containing CUI within **Simtenant Alpha Aerospace LLC (synthetic)** in accordance with NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 (Family 3.8) and CMMC L2 requirements.

## 2. Scope

This policy applies to all digital and physical media that contain, process, or are used to transmit CUI within the single_enclave boundary.

## 3. Roles and Responsibilities

| Role | Name | Responsibility |
|------|------|----------------|
| ISSO | Fixture Person One, ISSO, person.one@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Define media protection standards |
| IT Director | Fixture Person Four, IT Director, person.four@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Implement media controls and sanitization procedures |
| Facilities Manager | Fixture Person Seven, Facilities Manager, person.seven@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Secure physical media storage |

## 4. Policy Statements

### 4.1 Media Protection (3.8.1, 3.8.2)

- CUI media shall be protected using physical and logical access controls
- Access to CUI media shall be restricted to authorized personnel
- Digital media containing CUI shall be encrypted using FIPS 140-2 validated cryptography

### 4.2 Media Marking (3.8.4)

- All media containing CUI shall be marked with appropriate CUI markings
- Markings shall follow DoD CUI marking guidelines

### 4.3 Media Transport (3.8.5, 3.8.6)

- CUI media in transit shall be physically protected (locked containers, secure shipping)
- Digital transport of CUI shall use encrypted channels (TLS 1.2+, encrypted email)
- CUI shall not be transmitted over unencrypted channels

### 4.4 Media Sanitization (3.8.3)

- Media shall be sanitized before disposal or reuse using **NIST SP 800-88 Purge** guidelines
- Sanitization records shall be maintained for audit purposes
- Sanitization methods shall be appropriate to the media type and sensitivity

### 4.5 Media Storage (3.8.7, 3.8.8, 3.8.9)

- CUI media shall be stored in controlled areas
- Backup media shall be stored in a separate location from primary systems
- CUI on mobile devices shall be encrypted at rest

## 5. Review

This policy shall be reviewed every **12** months. Next scheduled review: **2027-02-01**.

This procedure establishes the personnel screening requirements for **Simtenant Alpha Aerospace LLC (synthetic)** to ensure that all individuals are screened prior to being authorized access to systems containing Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), in accordance with NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 control 3.9.1 and CMMC L2 requirements.

## 2. Scope

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, third-party personnel, and service accounts requiring access to CUI systems within the single_enclave boundary, including the cloud_only deployment posture operating in the gcc_high cloud environment.

## 3. Roles and Responsibilities

| Role | Name | Responsibility |
|------|------|----------------|
| HR Representative | Fixture Person Five, HR Representative, person.five@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Coordinate and document screening activities |
| ISSO | Fixture Person One, ISSO, person.one@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Verify screening completion before access provisioning |
| System Owner (AO) | Fixture Person Two, System Owner, person.two@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Authorize CUI access after all screening elements are documented |

## 4. Screening Criteria

All personnel must satisfy the following seven screening elements before CUI access is authorized:

### 4.1 Identity Verification

Government-issued photo identification must be verified and documented. Acceptable forms include a valid passport, driver's license, or state-issued identification card.

### 4.2 Citizenship and Immigration Status

Citizenship or lawful immigration status must be verified and documented.

### 4.3 Professional History Verification

Employment history for the prior seven years must be verified through direct employer contact or a qualified third-party investigation service.

### 4.4 Background Investigation

One of the following must be completed and documented:
- **Direct-knowledge attestation** by the Authorizing Official (see Section 6, Small-Organization Provision)
- **Third-party background investigation** conducted by a qualified investigation service

### 4.5 Self-Attestation

The individual must provide a signed self-attestation covering:
- Criminal history disclosure
- OFAC (Office of Foreign Assets Control) sanctions list clearance

### 4.6 CUI Acknowledgment

The individual must sign a CUI handling acknowledgment per 32 CFR Part 2002, confirming understanding of responsibilities for protecting CUI.

### 4.7 Authorizing Official Sign-Off

The Authorizing Official (Fixture Person Two, System Owner, person.two@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us) must review all completed screening elements and provide documented sign-off before CUI access is provisioned.

## 5. Authorization Gate

No account provisioning or CUI access shall be granted until all seven screening elements in Section 4 are completed and documented. The Authorizing Official sign-off (Section 4.7) is the final gate and must occur after all other elements are satisfactorily documented.

## 6. Small-Organization Provision

For organizations where the Authorizing Official has direct, firsthand knowledge of an individual's background (e.g., founder-level relationships), the following alternative is permitted:
- The Authorizing Official provides a written direct-knowledge attestation documenting the basis of their personal knowledge
- The individual provides a mutual attestation acknowledging their screening status
- Both attestations must be signed, dated, and retained per Section 7

This provision does not waive the requirements for identity verification (4.1), citizenship verification (4.2), CUI acknowledgment (4.6), or AO sign-off (4.7).

## 7. Documentation and Retention

The following evidence elements must be maintained for each individual screened:

1. Government-issued photo ID (copy)
2. Citizenship/immigration verification record
3. Professional history verification results
4. Background investigation report or direct-knowledge attestation
5. Signed self-attestation (criminal history, OFAC)
6. Signed CUI handling acknowledgment
7. Authorizing Official sign-off record

All screening records shall be retained for **6** years per 6 years per 32 CFR 170.16.

## 8. Reassessment

Personnel screening shall be reassessed every **5** years. Additionally, reassessment shall be triggered by any of the following events:

- Criminal arrest or conviction
- Role change with elevated CUI access
- Organizational ownership or control change

## 9. Third-Party Personnel

Third-party personnel, including contractors and subcontractors, are subject to the same screening requirements as organizational employees. Additionally:
- A non-disclosure agreement (NDA) covering CUI handling must be executed prior to access authorization
- The sponsoring organization must verify that screening has been completed before requesting access provisioning

## 10. Tooling Reference

Personnel screening status is tracked in the Personnel card Screening sub-feature of the compliance tooling. Screening completion status must be current before access provisioning workflows are executed.

## 11. Enforcement / Consequence of Non-Compliance

Failure to complete required screening elements will result in denial or revocation of CUI system access. Personnel who circumvent screening requirements or provide false information during the screening process are subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination, and may be reported to relevant authorities.

## 12. Review

This procedure shall be reviewed every **12** months. Next scheduled review: **2027-02-01**.

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, third-party personnel, and service accounts within the single_enclave boundary operating in the cloud_only deployment posture and the gcc_high cloud environment. | System Owner (AO) | Fixture Person Two, System Owner, person.two@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Authorize access changes and review completion of all actions |

## 4. Immediate Actions (typically within 1 business hour)

Upon notification of a personnel termination or for-cause separation, the following actions shall be completed typically within 1 business hour:

### 4.1 Notification

HR Representative notifies the ISSO and System Owner of the personnel action, including the type (termination, transfer, role change) and effective timing.

### 4.2 Disable Identity Provider Account

The departing individual's entra_native account shall be disabled to prevent new authentication.

### 4.3 Revoke Active Sessions

All active sessions (Microsoft 365, VPN, remote access) shall be revoked to terminate any currently authenticated access.

### 4.4 Remove Conditional Access Policy Scope

The individual shall be removed from all Conditional Access policy groups that grant CUI system access.

### 4.5 Disable Service Account Credentials

Any service account credentials, API keys, or shared secrets associated with the individual shall be rotated or disabled.

## 5. Near-Term Actions (typically within 1 business day)

The following actions shall be completed typically within 1 business day of the personnel action:

### 5.1 CUI Access Review

A comprehensive review of all CUI access grants shall be conducted to identify and document all systems, applications, and data repositories the individual had access to.

### 5.2 Email and OneDrive Preservation

The individual's Exchange Online mailbox and OneDrive for Business content shall be placed on litigation hold or exported for preservation in accordance with organizational retention requirements.

### 5.3 Data Access Review Trigger

A review shall be initiated to determine whether the individual accessed, downloaded, or transferred CUI data in the period preceding the personnel action.

### 5.4 License Unassignment

Microsoft 365 and other SaaS licenses assigned to the individual shall be unassigned and returned to the license pool.

### 5.5 Account Marked for Deletion

The disabled account shall be marked for deletion following the 30-day soft delete period, during which recovery remains possible if needed for investigation purposes.

## 6. Property Return

All organizational property shall be returned and documented using the following chain of custody record:

| Item | Serial/ID | Returned To | Date | Condition | Signature |
|------|-----------|-------------|------|-----------|-----------|
| Laptop/Workstation | | | | | |
| Mobile Device | | | | | |
| Access Badges/Cards | | | | | |
| Hardware Tokens/Keys | | | | | |
| Removable Media | | | | | |
| Other Equipment | | | | | |

All credentials, including passwords, PINs, and authentication tokens, shall be collected or confirmed as revoked.

## 7. Transfer-Specific Provisions

For personnel transferring between roles within the organization:

- **Access Review:** Current CUI access grants shall be reviewed against the requirements of the new role
- **Access Removal:** CUI access not required for the new role shall be revoked prior to the transfer effective date
- **Access Addition:** New CUI access required for the new role shall follow the standard screening and authorization process (EDC-POL-009)
- **Manager Authorization:** The receiving manager must authorize any new access grants in writing

## 8. SLA Enforcement

Time-bound expectations for immediate (typically 1 business hour) and near-term (typically 1 business day) actions are tracked through the compliance tooling. Elapsed time from notification to completion is recorded for each action item. SLA breaches shall be documented, including the reason for delay and any compensating controls applied during the extended period.

## 9. Sample Execution Provision

In the absence of actual termination events during an assessment period, procedural sample executions shall be conducted and documented to demonstrate the organization's capability to execute this procedure. Sample executions count as evidence of procedural readiness for assessment purposes.

## 10. Tooling Reference

Personnel termination and transfer actions are tracked through the Offboarding workflow in the compliance tooling. The procedural overlay artifact documents each step's completion status. entra_native audit log correlation provides independent verification of technical access revocation timing.

## 11. Documentation and Retention

All personnel action records, including notification timestamps, access revocation evidence, property return documentation, and completion confirmations, shall be retained for **6** years per 6 years per 32 CFR 170.16.

## 12. Enforcement / Consequence of Non-Compliance

Failure to execute personnel termination or transfer actions within the specified timeframes may result in unauthorized CUI access and constitutes a security incident. Personnel responsible for executing these procedures who fail to comply are subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination. All SLA breaches shall be documented and reported to the Authorizing Official.

## 13. Review

This procedure shall be reviewed every **12** months. Next scheduled review: **2027-02-01**.

This policy applies to all information systems, assets, operations, and individuals within the single_enclave boundary that process, store, or transmit CUI, including the cloud_only deployment posture operating in the gcc_high cloud environment.

| Role | Name | Responsibility |
|------|------|----------------|
| ISSO | Fixture Person One, ISSO, person.one@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Conduct and coordinate risk assessments |
| System Owner (AO) | Fixture Person Two, System Owner, person.two@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Accept or mitigate identified risks |
| Compliance Officer | Fixture Person Three, Compliance Officer, person.three@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Verify risk assessment completeness |

## 4. Policy Statements

### 4.1 Risk Assessment (3.11.1)

Simtenant Alpha Aerospace LLC (synthetic) shall periodically assess the risk to organizational operations, assets, and individuals resulting from the operation of information systems and the processing, storage, or transmission of CUI.

#### Methodology

Risk assessments shall be conducted in accordance with **NIST SP 800-30 Revision 1** (Rev 1 (September 2012)). The following NIST SP 800-30 appendices shall be used:

- Appendix D (Threat Sources)
- Appendix E (Threat Events)
- Appendix G (Likelihood Scale)
- Appendix H (Impact Scale)
- Appendix I (Composite Risk Matrix)

#### Frequency

Risk assessments shall be conducted on an annual 12-month cycle, with the assessment period anchored to the policy effective date. Additionally, risk assessments shall be triggered by any of the following events:

- Architectural changes to the CUI boundary
- New contracts with different CUI categories
- Tenant variant changes (e.g., GCC High to IL5)
- Significant security incidents affecting CUI
- Material changes in threat landscape

#### Required Assessment Activities

Each risk assessment shall include the following activities:
- Threat identification using NIST SP 800-30 Appendix D threat source taxonomy
- Vulnerability identification through technical scanning and organizational posture review
- Risk scoring using likelihood and impact scales (Appendices G and H)
- Composite risk computation using the risk matrix (Appendix I)
- Treatment recommendations for each identified risk

#### Required Outputs

Each risk assessment shall produce the following outputs:
- Risk register documenting all identified risks with likelihood, impact, and composite risk ratings
- Annual risk assessment report (EDC-DOC-001) summarizing findings and recommendations
- Authorizing Official sign-off accepting or directing treatment for each identified risk

#### Continuous-Versus-Annual Model

While formal risk assessments are conducted annually, the organization maintains continuous risk awareness through:
- Ongoing vulnerability scanning (per Section 4.2)
- Security incident analysis and trend monitoring
- Threat intelligence monitoring applicable to the CUI environment
- Readiness posture changes identified through the compliance tooling

Material risk changes identified through continuous monitoring shall trigger an event-driven risk assessment per the trigger events listed above.

#### Stakeholder Roles

- **Authorizing Official (Fixture Person Two, System Owner, person.two@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us):** Reviews and accepts residual risk; signs off on risk treatment decisions
- **Compliance Officer / IT Lead (Fixture Person Three, Compliance Officer, person.three@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us):** Coordinates assessment activities, maintains the risk register, and ensures assessment completeness
- **Small-Organization Provision:** In organizations where a single individual serves multiple roles, the Authorizing Official may serve as both risk assessor and risk acceptor, provided that the dual-role is documented and the assessment methodology is followed consistently

Risk assessments shall:
- Identify threats and vulnerabilities applicable to CUI systems
- Assess the likelihood and impact of potential security incidents
- Document risk determinations and recommended mitigations
- Be conducted at least annually and when significant changes occur

### 4.2 Vulnerability Scanning (3.11.2)

- Vulnerability scans shall be performed on a **monthly** basis
- Scans shall cover all in-scope systems, applications, and network devices
- Identified vulnerabilities shall be remediated based on severity:
  - Critical: within **14** days
  - High: within **30** days
  - Medium: within 90 days
  - Low: tracked and addressed during maintenance windows

### 4.3 Vulnerability Remediation (3.11.3)

- Vulnerabilities shall be remediated in accordance with organizational timelines
- Remediation activities shall be tracked to completion
- Risk acceptance decisions for unmitigated vulnerabilities shall be documented and approved by the System Owner
- Vulnerabilities that cannot be remediated within timelines may be tracked via Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M)

### 4A. Record Retention

All risk assessment records, including risk registers, assessment reports, vulnerability scan results, and treatment decisions, shall be retained for **6** years per 6 years per 32 CFR 170.16.

## 5. Review

This policy shall be reviewed every **12** months. Next scheduled review: **2027-02-01**.

## 6. Enforcement / Consequence of Non-Compliance

Failure to conduct required risk assessments within the specified timeframes or to address identified risks in accordance with this policy may result in disciplinary action. The Authorizing Official shall be notified of any non-compliance, and CUI system operations may be suspended until a current risk assessment is completed.

## 2. Scope

This policy applies to all information systems within the single_enclave boundary.

## 3. Roles and Responsibilities

| Role | Name | Responsibility |
|------|------|----------------|
| IT Director | Fixture Person Four, IT Director, person.four@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Implement integrity controls and patch management |

| System Owner | Fixture Person Two, System Owner, person.two@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us | Authorize system changes for flaw remediation |

## 4. Policy Statements

### 4.1 Flaw Remediation (3.14.1)

- Security flaws shall be identified, reported, and corrected in a timely manner
- Critical vulnerabilities: remediate within **14** days
- High vulnerabilities: remediate within **30** days
- Software updates and patches shall be tested before deployment where feasible

### 4.2 Malicious Code Protection (3.14.2)

- Malicious code protection shall be deployed at system entry points and workstations
- Anti-malware signatures shall be updated automatically
- Real-time scanning shall be enabled on all CUI systems
- Users shall not disable malicious code protection

### 4.3 Security Alert Monitoring (3.14.3)

- Security alerts, advisories, and directives shall be monitored from:
  - CISA (Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency)
  - Vendor security bulletins
  - Internal monitoring systems
- SIEM alerts: Microsoft Sentinel (simtenant-a-law-prod)
- Data connectors: Azure Active Directory, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Microsoft Defender for Office 365, Microsoft Defender for Identity, Azure Activity, Windows Security Events

### 4.4 System Monitoring (3.14.6, 3.14.7)

- Information systems shall be monitored for:
  - Unauthorized access attempts
  - Security-relevant configuration changes
  - Anomalous network traffic patterns
  - Indicators of compromise (IOCs)
- Monitoring activities shall be documented and alerts shall be investigated

### 4.5 Input Validation (3.14.5)

- System inputs shall be validated to prevent injection attacks and malformed data
- Input validation shall be applied at trust boundaries

### 4.6 Spam and Unsolicited Communications (3.14.4)

- Email and messaging systems shall implement spam filtering and malicious content detection
- Phishing protection mechanisms shall be enabled

## 5. Review

This policy shall be reviewed every **12** months. Next scheduled review: **2027-02-01**.

## 2. Purpose

This Incident Response Plan establishes the procedures for detecting, responding to, containing, eradicating, and recovering from security incidents affecting CUI systems operated by **Simtenant Alpha Aerospace LLC (synthetic)**.

## 3. Scope

This plan applies to all security incidents affecting information systems within the single_enclave boundary that process, store, or transmit CUI. This includes cloud_only environments hosted on the **gcc_high** tenant (simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us).

## 4. Incident Response Team

| ISSO | Fixture Person One, ISSO, person.one@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us |  | Security assessment and containment |

| HR Representative | Fixture Person Five, HR Representative, person.five@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us |  | Personnel-related incidents |

## 5. Incident Classification

| Severity | Description | Response Time | Notification |
|----------|-------------|---------------|-------------|
| **Critical** | Active CUI compromise, data exfiltration, ransomware | Immediate | IR Lead + System Owner + Legal within 30 min |
| **High** | Potential CUI exposure, unauthorized access to CUI system | Within 72 hour(s) | IR Lead + ISSO |
| **Medium** | Policy violation, suspicious activity, malware detection | Within 4 hours | ISSO |
| **Low** | Minor security event, no CUI impact | Within 24 hours | ISSO (documented) |

## 6. Incident Response Phases

### 6.1 Preparation

- Maintain incident response tools and forensic capabilities
- Conduct annual incident response training for IR team members
- Maintain contact lists for IR team, management, and external parties
- Ensure logging and monitoring are operational on all CUI systems
- Primary SIEM: Microsoft Sentinel (simtenant-a-law-prod)

### 6.2 Detection and Analysis

**Detection sources:**
- Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) alerts
- Endpoint detection and response (EDR) alerts
- User reports of suspicious activity
- Vulnerability scan results
- External threat intelligence feeds

**Analysis procedures:**
1. Verify the incident is genuine (not a false positive)
2. Determine the scope and severity using the classification above
3. Identify affected systems, data, and users
4. Determine whether CUI has been compromised
5. Document initial findings in the incident tracking system

### 6.3 Containment

**Short-term containment:**
- Isolate affected systems from the network
- Disable compromised user accounts
- Block malicious IP addresses or domains
- Preserve volatile evidence (memory dumps, network captures)

**Long-term containment:**
- Apply temporary mitigations (patches, configuration changes)
- Enhance monitoring on potentially affected systems
- Implement additional access controls as needed

### 6.4 Eradication

- Remove malware and unauthorized access mechanisms
- Patch exploited vulnerabilities
- Reset compromised credentials
- Verify eradication through scanning and monitoring

### 6.5 Recovery

- Restore systems from known-good backups
- Verify system integrity before returning to production
- Monitor recovered systems for signs of continued compromise
- Gradually return systems to normal operations
- Backup frequency: **Daily**

### 6.6 Post-Incident Activity

- Conduct lessons-learned review within 5 business days
- Document the complete incident timeline
- Identify root cause and contributing factors
- Update the IRP based on lessons learned
- Update detection rules and monitoring based on findings
- Retain incident documentation for a minimum of **365** days

## 7. External Reporting Requirements

### 7.1 DoD Reporting

For incidents involving CUI under DoD contracts:
- Report to DIBNet within 72 hours of discovery
- Preserve and protect images of affected systems for 90 days
- Provide support to DoD damage assessment activities

### 7.2 Law Enforcement

Contact law enforcement when criminal activity is suspected, with guidance from the Legal representative (Fixture Person Eight, Contracts Representative, person.eight@simtenant-a.onmicrosoft.us).
